name: personal-computer
description: Keeps personal data out of Claude: every tool output is scanned on your machine (OpenAI Privacy Filter and PII-Tracer), and output with personal data is processed by a private model you choose through anymodel, while Claude orchestrates.

agent.title: Private agent
agent.description: The anymodel agent that works with output containing personal data, by its name as in @anymodel:<name>. Add one with /plugin configure anymodel: a local model, or one on your own private server.

mode.title: When personal data is found
mode.description: private: the output is withheld and Claude asks your private agent for what it needs. mask: Claude gets the output with names, IBANs and the like replaced by placeholders. ask: you choose each time.

prompts.title: Check your prompts
prompts.description: Checks what you send to Claude, pasted text included. ask: with personal data in a prompt, you choose: mask it, send it as is, or cancel. mask: personal data in prompts is replaced by placeholders without asking. off: prompts are not checked.

detectors.title: Detection models
detectors.description: both: OpenAI Privacy Filter and PII-Tracer (most found; 3.7 GB on MLX, 8 GB on ONNX Runtime). opf: OpenAI Privacy Filter alone (2.6 GB, or 5.6 GB). pii-tracer: PII-Tracer alone (1.1 GB, or 2.4 GB). IBANs and card numbers are always found by their checksums. Run /personal-computer setup after a change.

runtime.title: Runs on
runtime.description: auto: MLX on a Mac with Apple silicon, ONNX Runtime elsewhere (Linux, and Windows inside WSL 2). mlx: MLX, Apple silicon only. onnx: ONNX Runtime on any of them; it needs more memory, up to about 30 GB on an output past 8,000 tokens. onnx-int8: 8-bit models on ONNX Runtime, a third of the download (2.5 GB); PII-Tracer then needs a quarter of the memory, and each model finds a little less (see the reference). gguf: PII-Tracer from Perplexity's own GGUF on your llama.cpp (llama-server on PATH, which picks its CPU or GPU build), OpenAI Privacy Filter on ONNX Runtime. Run /personal-computer setup after a change.
